vendors.name: Amazon RDS Proxy
vendors.offering: Managed DB proxy, now with end-to-end IAM authentication for RDS/Aurora MySQL and PostgreSQL
vendors.pricing: usage-based, per vCPU-hour (or per ACU-hour for Aurora Serverless), region-dependent

vendors.name: Teleport (Database Access / Machine & Workload Identity)
vendors.offering: Identity-aware proxy that uses IAM auth to RDS, issuing short-lived credentials
vendors.pricing: not public (quote-based; usage-based on monthly active users and Teleport Protected Resources, with each tbot machine-identity instance counted as a TPR, no separate per-MWI price)

vendors.name: StrongDM
vendors.offering: Infrastructure access proxy for databases, servers and Kubernetes with credential brokering
vendors.pricing: per user; third-party listings ~$50/user/month, AWS Marketplace Essentials $840/user/year

vendors.name: hoop.dev
vendors.offering: Identity-aware access gateway for databases including AWS RDS with IAM authentication

vendors.name: Aembit Workload IAM
vendors.offering: Secretless workload-to-service access with credential injection and access policies
vendors.pricing: free Starter (10 workloads); Teams/Enterprise price not confirmed on vendor page

paid_market_gaps.gap: Popular third-party clients and ORMs (Prisma, kafka-go, ArgoCD) lack native AWS IAM auth; vendors don't sell client-side fixes.
RDS IAM auth caps around 200 new connections/second; the AWS workaround, RDS Proxy, adds per-vCPU cost.
Access proxies that broker IAM DB auth (Teleport, StrongDM) are quote-based or seat-minimum, heavy for small teams.
API Gateway IAM (SigV4) invocation from generic tooling relies on per-tool support that is often missing.

wtp_evidence: Buyers pay for broad access platforms: Vendr reports a StrongDM median of ~$33k/yr across 58 purchases, and its buyer guide shows a ~$71k average contract value that large deals skew upward. IAM itself is usable at no additional charge per AWS's RDS docs, so the per-client auth plumbing has no paid line item to displace.
bundling_note: AWS already ships IAM auth for RDS/MSK/Redshift/API Gateway plus free open-source signers in every major language and RDS Proxy, so remaining gaps get closed by AWS or OSS maintainers.
summary: Little standalone opening: the need is client-library plumbing that AWS and open source fill for free. Money only exists inside broader access-proxy platforms (Teleport, StrongDM), a crowded segment; at most a developer-tool feature, not a startup.
